questions.q: According to Harari, what allowed humans to dominate other species?
a: The ability to cooperate through shared stories
The ability to use tools more skillfully than others
A larger brain and stronger physical endurance
The capacity to live in a wider range of climates
questions.why: Lesson 1 says shared narratives let humans collaborate on a massive scale, which drove their evolutionary success.

questions.q: Which narrative does Harari call the dominant one in the world today?
a: Humanism
Nationalism
Dataism
Transhumanism
questions.why: Lesson 2 says humanism is the story that currently dominates, with liberalism as its most common variant.

questions.q: What does humanism treat as humanity's greatest asset?
a: Individual freedom
Scientific progress
Economic growth
Religious faith
questions.why: Lesson 2 says humanism places humans at the center and prizes individual freedom above all.

a: Merging humans with technology to enhance our abilities
Replacing human workers entirely with algorithms
Returning to a simpler life before modern technology
Letting data systems run society without human input
questions.why: Lesson 3 says transhumanism wants people to combine with technology so they can keep pace with algorithms.

questions.q: What does dataism suggest humans should do?
a: Step aside and let algorithms become as powerful as possible
Limit algorithms so human judgment always comes first
Use data only to improve health and recreation
Merge with machines to compete against algorithms
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes dataism as letting algorithms develop freely, potentially leaving humans behind.
